For fat loss, low-fat diets beat low-carb diets handily, new research finds
In the second 'related' bit on the left side of the article it says the exact opposite - Study: Low-carb diet beats low fat for weight loss and heart health.

I wonder who funded this study. And got a newspaper to write about it.

From the original article's abstract (because I'm not paying to read it), this study was poorly constructed and does not prove anything.

The published article states that they only had people on low-fat v low-carb conditions for 6 days, which is not enough for your body to adjust to a low-carb diet and enter ketosis. Dieting just doesn't start to work in 6 days. This also means there was no control group, making me further question the validity of their conclusions.

Further, they used this calculation for their DV ("body fat loss"): "the differerence between daily fat intake and net fat oxidation measured." Of course if you start with a big number (low-carb and an undocumented amount of fat) and small number (low-fat and an undocumented amount of carbs) and subtract from them, the smaller number will be smaller.

They then used these incredibly short-term results to mathematically conceptualize (aka graph a line) to predict long-term results which may or may not be accurate. Am I missing something here?

tl:dr shitty study; shitty conclusions

I agree with you, also it was funded by NIH, so tax payers funded it. Once I read they extrapolated two weeks to six months I just laughed and stopped reading, and I have free access to the paper.

I don't believe they are trying to push people to ketosis, which I think is a dumb way to diet, just cut their carbs to a much lower level.

It surprises me that this is in Cell Metabolism, a high impact and generally great journal.

It is disconcerting when reputable journals publish such questionable studies and tax dollars pay for it.

I don't trust journalist when reporting scientific study. Most of the time they obscure the result and do not even provide a good parameter to give the reader a better understanding about the subject. Here's the actual study (not in paywall).

Please note that the subjects are people with obesity and is focused as such. They are, however, more controlled compared to other study but their study only last for few weeks. During the period of study, both diets resulted to almost the same fat loss. However, when they put their data in simulated 6 months period, low fat diet yielded better fat loss if compare calorie per calorie with low carb diet. But before we go, changing our diet, let me share you their warning first.

Translation of our results to real-world weight-loss diets for treatment of obesity is limited since the experimental design and model simulations relied on strict control of food intake, which is unrealistic in free-living individuals. While our results suggest that the experimental reduced-fat diet was more effective at inducing body fat loss than the reduced-carbohydrate diet, diet adherence was strictly enforced. We did not address whether it would be easier to adhere to a reduced-fat or a reduced-carbohydrate diet under free-living conditions. Since diet adherence is likely the most important determinant of body fat loss, we suspect that previously observed differences in weight loss and body fat change during outpatient diet interventions (Foster et al., 2010, Gardner et al., 2007, Shai et al., 2008) were primarily due to differences in overall calorie intake rather than any metabolic advantage of a low-carbohydrate diet.
